        ### Question
        A 65-year-old man presents to the emergency department with abdominal pain and a pulsatile abdominal mass. Further examination of the mass shows that it is an abdominal aortic aneurysm. A computed tomography scan with contrast reveals an incidental finding of a horseshoe kidney, and the surgeon is informed of this finding prior to operating on the aneurysm. Which of the following may complicate the surgical approach in this patient?

        ### Options
        opa. Abnormal relationship between the kidney and the superior mesenteric artery
opb. Anomalous origins of multiple renal arteries
opc. Low glomerular filtration rate due to unilateral renal agenesis
opd. Proximity of the fused kidney to the celiac artery
ope. There are no additional complications

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Horseshoe kidney" -> "fusion of the lower poles of the kidneys" -> "abnormal relationship between the kidney and surrounding structures" -> 80% CHAIN: "Horseshoe kidney" -> "anomalous origins of multiple renal arteries" -> "complicated vascular anatomy during surgery" -> 75% CHAIN: "Horseshoe kidney" -> "fusion of the kidneys" -> "proximity of the fused kidney to major blood vessels" -> "complicated surgical approach" -> 80%
